statement: The function rectangle_mesh is defined in fedoo/mesh/simple.py with signature rectangle_mesh(nx=11, ny=11, x_min=0, x_max=1, y_min=0, y_max=1, elm_type="quad4", ndim=None, name="") and its docstring says "Create a rectangular Mesh".
In the source docstring, nx and ny are "Numbers of nodes in the x and y axes (default = 11)", i.e. node counts, not element counts.
The elm_type parameter accepts {'tri3', 'quad4', 'quad8', 'quad9'} with default 'quad4', described as 'The type of the element generated (default=\'quad4\')'.
The source docstring documents element types including "'quad4' -- 4 node quadrangular mesh".
The function returns a Mesh built as Mesh(crd, elm, elm_type, node_sets, {}, ndim, name).
The mesh nodes are generated by np.meshgrid of np.linspace(x_min, x_max, nx) and np.linspace(y_min, y_max, ny), so the rectangle spans [x_min, x_max] × [y_min, y_max].
The function also creates node sets named 'bottom', 'top', 'left', 'right' for the four sides of the rectangle (used for boundary conditions).

The official Sphinx API reference lists the signature rectangle_mesh(nx=11, ny=11, x_min=0, x_max=1, y_min=0, y_max=1, elm_type='quad4', ndim=None, name='') and states it "Create[s] a rectangular Mesh" returning a Mesh.
The API reference page describes nx as 'int — Numbers of nodes in the x and y axes (default = 11)'.
The mesh guide page (Main_documentation_fedoo/mesh.html) lists rectangle_mesh in the fedoo.mesh generator table as "rectangle_mesh([nx, ny, x_min, x_max, ...])".

The OKF documentation guide states the verified fedoo 1.0.1 signature: rectangle_mesh(nx=11, ny=11, x_min=0, x_max=1, y_min=0, y_max=1, elm_type="quad4", ndim=None, name=""); nx/ny are node counts; elm_type in tri3/tri6/quad4/quad8/quad9.
The OKF guide gives a verified size check: rectangle_mesh(5, 240, 23, 25, 0, 180) → 1200 nodes / 956 quad4 / 3824 Gauss points on fedoo 1.0.1.
The simplest exact call, used in the fedoo post-processing docstring example, is: mesh = fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh() (default 11×11 quad4 unit square).
The docs/user_problems.rst guide shows the same minimal call mesh = fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh() followed by pb.bc.add('Dirichlet', 'left', ...) and ('right', ...), illustrating the default node sets.
The boundary_conditions docs show a full keyword call: mesh_rect = fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh(nx=11, ny=21, x_min=0, x_max=1, y_min=0, y_max=1, elm_type='quad4', name='Domain').
The 01-simple example poison_eq.py builds the Poisson-equation domain with the default call mesh = fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh().
The 02-constraints example rigid_tie.py builds its mesh with the default call mesh = fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh().
The 01-simple modal_analysis.py example builds a 3D (ndim=3) quad4 rectangle: fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh(nx=15, ny=15, x_min=0.0, x_max=length, y_min=0.0, y_max=length, elm_type="quad4", ndim=3).
The plasticity example 2DplasticBending.py builds its beam with fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh(nx=41, ny=21, x_min=0, x_max=L, y_min=0, y_max=h, elm_type="quad4", ...).
The 02-constraints example disk_rectangle_contact.py builds the rectangle with fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh(nx=11, ny=21, x_min=0, x_max=L, y_min=0, y_max=h, elm_type="quad4", name="Domain").
The contact penalty example disk_rectangle.py builds its rectangle mesh with fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh( at line 24.
The tube compression IPC example uses a positional argument call: mesh = fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh(5, 240, 23, 25, 0, 180) (5×240 nodes, x∈[23,25], y∈[0,180]).
The adaptive example hessian_recovery.py shows a triangular variant: mesh = fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh(nx=51, ny=51, elm_type="tri3").
The lattice_beam example uses fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh(n, n, x_max=100, y_max=100, ndim=ndim) passed to fd.mesh.extract_edges to build a lattice.
The Hertz axisymmetric benchmark uses fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh( for both the substrate (line 82) and indenter (line 98) meshes.
The fedoo test suite calls it with ndim for 3D problems, e.g. mesh=fd.mesh.rectangle_mesh(2, 2, elm_type="quad4", ndim=3).
The docs/user_problems.rst example applies Dirichlet BCs on the default node sets: problem.bc.add("Dirichlet", "left", "U", 0) and problem.bc.add("Dirichlet", "right", "U", 1).
